name: cc-enslaver
description: A Claude Code plugin and LLM-agnostic rule pack that enforces systematic thinking, verified citations, and root-cause analysis — eliminating reactive, lazy AI behavior. v0.27.0 closes the three items v0.26 recorded as 'known, not fixed', each decided by evidence rather than preference. (1) The shell tokeniser now follows the SHELL, not the host OS: v0.25.1 disabled backslash escaping when os.name == 'nt', but measuring the shell Claude Code actually runs on Windows (Git Bash / MSYS, bash 5.2.37) showed the branch wrong in both directions — an unquoted drive path loses its separators in the real shell too, so it rescued nothing, while `git push --for\ce` reached git as --force with the guard seeing an unrecognised token. That live force-push bypass is closed; a drive path must be QUOTED. (2) Stop layer (h) now carries two verdicts instead of one: 'attributable' (generous, for presence — a false negative blocks a reply for a tldr that is visibly present) and 'countable' (conservative, for the 160-char measurement). They differ only on CommonMark lazy continuation, which is exactly why v0.26 could not implement it; it is implemented now. (3) Stop layer (i) settles only groups the agent has actually been SHOWN — the primary path used to ack every pending group while the grace path acked only the presented set, and that inconsistency was itself the bypass. A group is named by one block, then settled by the next reply's marker: one INFORMED answer per group. That is a strictness increase, recorded as such. Tests 543 → 556. Prior — v0.26.0 was a fourth-round audit release: it reviewed the PREVIOUS release's own fix diff and replaced the mechanism instead of the symptoms. 37 findings, 33 reproduced by first-party runtime probes, collapsing into three root causes — the detector encoded a SPELLING rather than the concept (a `#` inside a URL counted as a comment, so one neighbouring `https://api.example.com` line disabled the secret detector; block structure was read from PHYSICAL lines, which regressed nested try/except from deny to allow while claiming the opposite); hardening was scoped to the observed instance rather than the class; and the claim outran the change (four tests passed unchanged on the pre-fix tree, and the self-rewritability invariant claimed to cover the whole tree while globbing half of it — six of the ten test modules were self-locked). Fixed as four shared models — lib/srclex (tolerant source lexer: comments vs docstrings vs data literals), lib/mdctx (markdown fence/blockquote context, now shared by both halves of Stop layer (h)), lib/shellcmd (segments → argv → git subcommand / python script operand), and a schema-driven state normaliser — rather than ~30 individual patches. The fix was then RE-AUDITED before shipping and 8 further defects in the NEW code were found and fixed, one of which would have been a regression ($(git push --force) was caught by the old text heuristic purely by accident). Tests 378 → 543 across two audit rounds; the first round's 43 failures + 3 errors replay on the pre-fix tree. A SECOND round of 16 parallel read-only reviews (15 reported; the sync-gate lens returned nothing and is recorded as not run) then fixed 20+ further confirmed defects at the root — a bare triple-quoted expression counting as a docstring and so silencing the secret detector, a lone CR letting a comment swallow the rest of a file, the tldr length check ignoring line attribution on continuation lines (the same two-halves-disagree bug one level down), 'far from done' reading as a completion and BLOCKING honest failure reports, a JSONDecodeError silently wiping a session's entire state, six Bash patterns still matching raw text while force-push used a parse model, and a registration inside `false && …` earning read credit for a command the shell never runs. It also caught five stale test counts and two false claims in THIS release's own notes — the gate had exempted the current release's narrative as 'history' while it describes the release being shipped. Prior — v0.24 health audit: a full architecture review plus multi-path adversarial model review (every finding re-verified with a runtime probe; red-first regression tests, 310 → 323) fixed 10 confirmed defects, 3 HIGH, zero new features. Its HIGH fixes: Windows state saves were silently lost to the plugin's OWN lock-free readers (os.replace vs an open reader → PermissionError → failing-open → the mutation vanished, with orphan .tmp debris as live evidence; read accessors now share the per-session lock, save() retries against non-cooperating external readers, load() retries transient OSError, gc sweeps day-old orphan tmp files); the layer-(i) sync acknowledgement was lost in the one-shot grace window (the primary block → 同步核对-recovery flow never persisted the ack, so an answered group re-blocked later — the grace path now reads the reply and acks); and a DENIED Write of a new file still registered its target as 'read', granting read-before-edit authorization for content the agent never saw. MED fixes: the rolling-patch counter's decide-and-record is now one atomic locked operation; rule 10 no longer flags Python forward-reference annotations (password: "SecretStr" — pure-alpha CamelCase values are type names, not secrets); rule 11 no longer flags URL routes (https://host/home/alice/… — a hostname-glued /home/ segment is a route; file:///home/… still denies); requirements*.txt / constraints*.txt are now scannable despite .txt (dependency manifests are a real credential-leak vector) while .asciidoc joins the prose exemption; and a stale rolling counter no longer survives delete-and-recreate. The three write branches of read_guard were deduplicated into one shared content-check pipeline, making the branch-drift bug class structurally impossible. Prior: v0.23 added rule 12 (repo-wide sync: per-project sync-gate.toml co-update groups enforced at Stop layer (i) with a marker escape, plus the repo-refresh whole-repo audit skill), a 160-char-per-item TL;DR cap at layer (h), and two HIGH production fixes (edit-gated Stop layers never fired — no turn_count in production payloads; session-state lost-update race); v0.22 added write-time content detectors rules 10 (no non-essential hardcoding) and 11 (no non-essential path dependency), PreToolUse-only with a why-comment escape hatch; v0.22.2 added the version-drift gate pinning every manifest version pointer, the README badge, and the newest CHANGELOG heading to plugin.json. English remains the i18n skeleton and source of truth (rules/ + prompts/ at the root, default injection); Chinese is a first-class translation (rules/zh/ + prompts/zh/, via CC_ENSLAVER_LANG=zh), with drift CI-blocked by i18n_check.py + test_i18n_sync.py.
